story.hero.heading: Build uncompromising apps
story.hero.under: Your agent asks what you want to make, builds it, and gives you a public link for 24 hours. No account or install needed.
story.u.heading: What does uncompromising mean?
story.u.p1: Most apps are built on compromises. There was never enough time, so something had to give.
story.u.p2: Accessibility waited for version two. Security became a ticket. Everyone’s data went into one database, because one each was too much work.
story.u.p3: Building apps with AI means we no longer have to cut corners.
story.u.p4: But agents cut corners too, unless the careful way is also the easy way. CARLOS makes it the easy way. So one app can be all of these at once.
story.u.figure: The usual app, drawn as a square with its corners cut off: accessibility later, one region, one shared database and nightly backups. Beside it, a CARLOS app is a circle, with no corners to cut.
story.c1.heading: Everything it needs is inside.
story.c1.body: A CARLOS app is one file: web server, database, background jobs and interface.
story.c1.loose: Nothing to wire together, so nothing to come loose.
story.c1.poke: Go on, give it a poke.
story.c1.poked: It squishes and springs back. Nothing falls out.
story.c1.figure: On one side, the usual pile of thirteen parts. On the other, one CARLOS app: its web server, database, jobs and interface sit inside its ring.
story.c2.heading: One each.
story.c2.body: Every customer gets their own copy of the app, with their own database inside it.
story.c2.wall: What keeps two customers apart is a wall, not a line in a query.
story.c2.stopped: A request from Acme’s copy for Birch’s data has nowhere to go.
story.c2.figure: One app divides into a copy for each customer: Acme, Birch and Cobalt, each inside its own ring. A request from Acme’s copy for Birch’s data stops at Birch’s ring.
